Definition: a pole (as a mast or flagstaff)
BiblicalUsage: A pole is a mast at sea and a beacon on a hill. Tyre's ships had masts of cedar from Lebanon, and Isaiah says the remnant shall be left as a beacon upon the top of a mountain and as an ensign on a hill.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the image is lonely on purpose: a pole left standing after the fleet is gone, and a people left standing after the army has fled.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
